newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police jam Bonn streets to protest cutbacks.
newsitem.headline: German police jam Bonn streets to protest cutbacks.

text.p: About 5,000 German police, firemen and other civil servants marched through Bonn's government quarter on Tuesday to protest against cutbacks by state and federal governments.

Blowing whistles and chanting anti-government slogans, the uniformed police officers led the demonstration. Arriving in Bonn from across Germany, they blocked one of the city's busiest traffic arteries for about an hour.
"Helmut, if you take the shirt off our backs, we'll take the pants off of you," they chanted at one point.
"Crime is rising, our pay is falling," read one banner.

The unions were demonstrating against government proposals to raise the retirement age for police and fire fighters from 60 to 61 and denouced Chancellor Helmut Kohl for trying to push Germany into Europe's single currency at their expense.

They were also protesting against suggestions made by leaders in Kohl's centre-right government on cutting pay for night and weekend shifts as well as reducing bonus compensation for dangerous assignments.
"Keep you paws off the bonus pay for police and firefighters," said one police union leader Dieter Berberich in a speech to the crowd.

One protester held a poster reading "Theo, just imagine someone broke into your house and no one came to help" -- referring to Finance Minister Theo Waigel and his embattled efforts to reduce government spending.
"Don't destroy the civil servants with budget cuts" read another banner.
While police union leaders said about 5,000 took part in the demonstration, Bonn police offices escorting the protest said there were about 3,000.
Several speakers drew loud applause for their pointed attacks on Kohl's government at the rally held just across the street from his chancellery.
"The German police union is now demonstrating publicly on the streets against the policies of massive wage cuts, cuts in social standing and a humbling of its members," said Berberich.
"We are not only trying to protect our pay, but we are talking about security," he added in a speech. "And we all have a right to that."
Berberich said Kohl's government was desperately trying to meet the Maastricht Treaty criteria on monetary union and was blind to the damage it was causing.

"With unprecedented thievery, the coalition is trying to cash in now on the mistakes it has made over many past years," he said. "Kohl and his government only see one political goal of introducing the ruo and fulfilling the euro criteria at any cost."
The demonstration, timed just as the rush hour in Bonn was beginning at 3 p.m., blocked traffic from several kilometres (miles) on a key artery through the government quarter.

"What kind of employer first sucks the best years out of a worker and then breaks its promise to allow workers to retire when agreed," Berberich said. "That is a breach of trust. That is exploitation."
